front: What did the NAACL 2025 Vectara study find about chunking vs. embedding model choice?
back: Testing 25 chunking configurations against 48 embedding models, chunking configuration influenced retrieval quality as much as, or more than, the embedding model choice.

front: What's the recommended default chunking strategy, and why?
back: Recursive chunking, 256-512 tokens with ~10-20% overlap — zero-cost (no embedding/LLM calls), respects natural boundaries, and wins on end-to-end accuracy (69%) in 2026 benchmarks despite lower raw recall than semantic chunking.

front: Semantic chunking measured recall vs. end-to-end accuracy, compared to recursive?
back: Semantic: 91.9% recall but only 54% end-to-end accuracy. Recursive: 85-89% recall but 69% accuracy. Semantic fragments can be topically pure but too small to fully answer from (avg. ~43 tokens).

front: What does late chunking do differently from every other chunking method?
back: It embeds the entire document first (full self-attention across all tokens), then splits the resulting token-level embeddings into chunks afterward — so each chunk's embedding stays grounded in whole-document context, unlike methods that embed chunks in isolation.

front: What is proposition-based chunking, and what model does the page use for it?
back: Decomposing text into atomic, self-contained factual statements (pronouns resolved, implicit subjects spelled out) — introduced by Dense X Retrieval (Chen et al., 2023). Uses `chentong00/propositionizer-wiki-flan-t5-large`, a 780M-param T5 model that runs locally for free.

front: How does small-to-big/parent-document retrieval resolve the precision-vs-context tradeoff?
back: It embeds and indexes small child chunks for precise matching, but returns the larger linked parent chunk to generation — small chunks retrieve precisely, big chunks carry context.

front: What does adaptive chunking actually do, as opposed to being a chunking technique itself?
back: It's a strategy selector, not a chunking method — it runs several candidate strategies against a document, scores each (e.g. via coherence), and picks the winner per document, which matters for genuinely mixed-format corpora.

front: What does Anthropic's Contextual Retrieval do, and what were its measured gains?
back: It prepends an LLM-generated summary blurb (50-100 tokens) to each chunk before embedding, one cacheable LLM call per chunk — cutting retrieval failures 49% alone and 67% combined with reranking.
